captions.text: Big Board gives a duty supervisor or department coordinator a shared
view of operational information.
From the board, use the plus icon at the upper right to open Add Widget.
Choose Personnel Status Summary, Personnel Staffing Summary and Units Summary.
After adding them, scroll to the three rendered panels.
This fictional department already has calls, units and a personnel
list elsewhere on its board.
These summary panels provide counts that you can compare with those detailed views.
Read Personnel Status and Personnel Staffing as separate measures.
Here, Standing By shows fourteen in the status panel.
Staffing shows three Available, one Delayed, two Unavailable,
zero Committed and eight On Shift.
The same fourteen people are being described in different ways.
A Standing By status therefore does not mean that fourteen
people have Available staffing.
Keep both panels visible when discussing the department's current staffing
picture, rather than treating one count as a substitute for the other.

scenes.title: Improve contrast and verify the visible result

captions.text: The colored personnel-status counts are difficult to distinguish
against this dark background.
Use the gear icon at the upper right to open configuration, then
select Personnel Status Widget.
On Personnel Status Summary Widget, turn Show Colors off.
This example keeps Font Size at fourteen points, with width and
height both set to four grid units.
Select Save and return to the board.
The Personnel Status numbers now use neutral light text, making
the zero values easier to see.

scenes.title: Read the staffing distribution without overinterpreting it

captions.text: In Personnel Staffing, compare all five rows.
Available is three, Delayed is one, Unavailable is two, Committed
is zero and On Shift is eight.
These totals describe the staffing values currently reported for the demo roster.
The panel does not identify which individuals make up each count.
Use it to spot a staffing question, then consult the personnel details
before making an assignment.
A count alone does not tell you a person's qualifications, current location
or suitability for a particular task.

scenes.title: Compare unit totals with individual states

captions.text: Units Summary shows eight total units, six Available, one
Responding and zero On Scene.
Scroll to the detailed Units table to see the individual names and State values.
Squad Three is Responding, Ambulance Sixty One is Released, and Reserve
Engine Fifty One is Out of Service.
Other rows say Available.
The summary groups underlying status categories, so its Available
number is not simply a count of rows containing that exact word.
Review the detailed states when selecting a specific resource.

scenes.title: Check the age of the underlying unit information

captions.text: The Units table also includes Station, Type and Updated.
In this recorded example, several unit updates are four, five or seven
days old, while the two training vehicles show one minute ago.
Those ages matter when interpreting a summary built from these states.
A visible count does not establish that every underlying report is recent.
Read Updated alongside State, and resolve stale information through your
department's normal status-reporting process before relying on the
board for an operational decision.

scenes.title: Reload and read back the saved preferences

captions.text: After saving, reload the board and return to the summary panels.
The neutral personnel-status counts remain visible.
Reopen configuration and select Personnel Status Widget again.
Show Colors is still off, and the form still shows fourteen points
and four-by-four grid dimensions.
This readback checks the setting that was actually saved.
Repeat that check on the display used by your team, and assess the text from
the distance where viewers will read it.

scenes.title: Use the same panels across different organizations

captions.text: These panels can support more than fire and E M S.
A security supervisor can compare staffing with patrol-unit states.
A search-and-rescue coordinator can review people and vehicles separately.
Community paramedicine and mental health response teams, wildland contractors
and industrial emergency response teams can use the same distinction between
personnel status, staffing and unit state.
Keep the labels meaningful to your department, use the detailed
lists to investigate the counts, and make sure the displayed
information is readable and current.
